about.title: Personal Injury Help in Daly City, California
about.longDescription: Daly City sits right where San Francisco gives way to the Peninsula, and a great deal of traffic passes through on its way somewhere else. I-280 carries the bulk of it, while Mission Street, John Daly Boulevard and Junipero Serra Boulevard handle the local flow between neighborhoods, the BART station and the shops around Westlake. Public records for 2025 list 257 injury collisions inside the city, with 336 people hurt and one life lost. Reports tend to rise on Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m., when commuters heading home and weekend traffic overlap on the same streets. If you were one of those 336 people, you probably have more questions than answers right now. Our team can help. We handle personal injury claims in San Mateo County and can walk through what happened to you. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Reaching out costs nothing and commits you to nothing, and it can bring some clarity to a confusing stretch of time.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Daly City Claim

items.title: Two years, and sometimes far less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. If a city, county or state agency may be responsible, the window to file a claim can shrink to six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you were partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by your share of the blame rather than eliminated altogether.

items.title: No statutory cap on pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain, lost enjoyment of life and emotional distress. Each case is valued on its own facts.

items.title: Contingency means no upfront cost
items.desc: We work on contingency. You pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: Where do injury crashes in Daly City tend to happen?
items.answer: Public collision records show the highest counts along I-280, Mission Street, John Daly Boulevard and Junipero Serra Boulevard. These are simply the corridors that carry the most traffic and therefore log the most reports. Records also show crashes peaking on Fridays between 6 and 8 p.m.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, the deadline is two years from the date of injury. When a government entity is involved, such as a claim over a city vehicle or roadway condition, you may have only six months to file a claim. We can confirm which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for what happened?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means being partly at fault reduces your recovery but does not bar it. If you were found 30 percent responsible, for example, your recovery would be reduced by 30 percent. Insurance companies sometimes overstate a person's share of fault, which is one reason people choose to speak with an attorney.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We handle personal injury claims directly in San Mateo County. We do not provide legal advice unrelated to your case or represent clients outside our scope of practice.

items.question: What will it cost me to talk with you?
items.answer: Your initial consultation is free. We work on contingency, which means no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case. The initial conversation is a chance to ask questions and decide whether you want to move forward.
